summary: The iOS app saves an ordered list of fabric members and walks it in the person's order (4 s per member, 10 s in all, a dropped member redialed after 1, 2 and 5 s before moving on); a member's refusal stops the walk and is shown with the member's saved name and what was refused, and each member other than the device's own is paired on its own, so each credential goes only to the member it was paired with

replay.detail: No daemon, store or projection code changed; only the iOS app's carrier, saved fabric targets, Fleet screen, pairing and their tests.

schema.detail: No database schema, claim or persisted daemon format change.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and fleet coordination are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: The app keeps the list under a new key (st3.fabric.members) and keeps the member that uses the device's own pairing under the old st3.fabric.target key, written as before, so an older app build keeps reaching that member with the credential it already sends there; a single target an older build saved reads as a list of one, and an older build's later change to that target is followed. Members paired on their own keep separate Keychain entries that an older build ignores. Each fabric dial now makes one unauthenticated capabilities read through the bridge to tell admission, refusal and an unreachable member apart; members need no change.

downtime.detail: No service restart; an app update.

manual.detail: No operator action. To use a second member, add it in Fleet › carrier and pair the phone with it there; the member needs a fabric grant for the phone as before.

recovery.detail: Revert the commit. An older build reads the old key as before; the new list key and per-member Keychain entries are then unused.
